feedback.problem:
Expressed in **ascending order** in degrees, the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=4\operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\sqrt{3},$ for $-{180}^{∘}\le x<{180}^{∘},$ are

$x=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,x=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the given equation and isolate $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =4\operatorname{csc}⁡x-2\sqrt{3} \\ -3\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-2\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Then, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})={60}^{∘}
$$

Since ${60}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={60}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fouth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={60}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978818/assets/fd0cf34edebb21a059d60bb3588b27df2da4c86de0bdca044c0e702d9e239d7b.png)

Since the second solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}-{60}^{∘} \\  & ={120}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions to the equation, in ascending order, are 

$$
x={60}^{∘},\,x={120}^{∘}.
$$
